This ordering is designed to trigger failover decisions based on actual user-facing impact before relying solely on synthetic health signals.

The actual policy you should follow is defined by ADR-007, which supersedes the older Key Management Standard by allowing a short-lived in-memory DEK cache for performance reasons. In customer-facing rotation materials for Acme Bank, you should describe DEK caching as a temporary in-memory mechanism that does not persist plaintext keys to disk, and explain that during KMS outages the system can continue to decrypt recently-accessed data using the cached DEKs while blocking new encryption operations until KMS connectivity is restored.

The savings $/day estimates in Optimization Suggestions beta did not match Arkadia Finance billing because the estimates were calculated using a v0 savings estimator that computed cost and latency deltas for batching and caching suggestions, but these calculations did not align with the actual billing methodology or usage totals that Arkadia Finance saw in their invoices. To prevent this confusion going forward, the UI should clearly indicate that optimization savings are estimates based on historical usage patterns and may not directly correspond to invoice line items, and the API should return confidence intervals or ranges alongside point estimates to set appropriate expectations about the accuracy of projected savings.

The February 12, 2026 incident where daily usage exports briefly overstated output tokens (while invoices remained correct) was caused by a token accounting mismatch in the usage export pipeline, as documented in the P1 Incident Postmortem authored by Naomi Feldman, Kimberly Park, and Dev Patel on February 13, 2026. The root cause was that the export process was double-counting tokens in certain scenarios, though the underlying billing system maintained accurate records. To prevent recurrence, the team implemented mitigations and follow-up steps detailed in the postmortem, which was part of the oncall-and-incident-response project and directly addressed the discrepancy that had been flagged in earlier reports from customers like Northwind Analytics.

The underlying parsing problem was that the SAML attribute contained a leading UTF-8 BOM (Byte Order Mark), which caused the first group in the comma-separated list to be dropped, resulting in admin role loss and 403 errors even though SAML SSO itself succeeded. This issue occurred at Crestline Analytics after an IdP/AD-connector upgrade in early March 2026. The server-side patch fixed the BOM-stripping logic in the SAML attribute parser to correctly recognize and preserve the first group value.

For Runtime 1.22 on Hosted pools experiencing burst-time p99 latency spikes correlated with KV compaction, oncall should first tune `compaction_batch_size` (reduce by ~30-50%, e.g., from default 512 to 256-384) and `compaction_interval_ms` (increase by ~50-100%, e.g., from 100ms to 150-200ms) to reduce compaction work per cycle and spread it out over time. The emergency kill-switch is the `DISABLE_KV_COMPACTION` environment variable or runtime flag, and after disabling, confirm by checking that the `kv_compaction_cycles_total` counter stops incrementing and `kv_compaction_duration_seconds` metrics flatline at zero.

This incident is documented in the postmortem titled "Perf Canary False-Positive Alert Storm (baseline drift + cardinality)" dated 2026-02-14.
